standard.title: Academic vocabulary
standard.description: identify and use vocabulary typical of academic texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify specialist and technical vocabulary and understand how vocabulary choices shape meaning and register (AC9E7LA08). They have not yet focused specifically on the cross-disciplinary vocabulary of academic writing — words that are not subject-specific but are characteristic of formal academic register across disciplines.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify vocabulary typical of academic texts and use it in their own writing, understanding how academic vocabulary creates precise information and conveys abstract ideas.

nodes.label: Identifying academic vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify vocabulary typical of academic texts — words used across disciplines to discuss evidence, reasoning and abstraction — and distinguish this from subject-specific technical vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least four academic vocabulary words in a provided academic text (e.g. 'evidence', 'consequence', 'contradiction', 'acknowledge') and explain that they are cross-disciplinary rather than subject-specific.
nodes.typical_width: Identify academic vocabulary across a range of academic texts on different topics; compare and contrast vocabulary choices in academic texts, considering how they create precise information or convey abstract ideas; distinguish academic vocabulary from technical vocabulary.
wider: Investigate how academic vocabulary differs across disciplines — comparing the language of a science report, a history essay and a literary analysis to identify shared academic vocabulary vs discipline-specific register
Examine how academic vocabulary items (e.g. 'evidence', 'analysis', 'significance') carry implicit disciplinary assumptions about what counts as valid knowledge
Compare the academic vocabulary in a text written for an expert audience with a version of the same content written for a general audience, and analyse what changes

response_modes.reason: Academic vocabulary is best understood as cross-disciplinary — it appears in science, history and English writing alike. Students who only encounter it in English contexts may not recognise its transferable nature. Multiple disciplinary contexts build this generalised understanding.

success_criteria: Identifies specific academic vocabulary words in a text and explains that they are typical of formal academic register.
Distinguishes academic vocabulary (cross-disciplinary) from technical vocabulary (subject-specific) with at least one example of each.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires accurate use of academic vocabulary in own writing. Students who have not grasped that academic vocabulary is cross-disciplinary will substitute subject-specific technical terms or informal equivalents — producing writing that fails to meet the academic register the descriptor requires.

nodes.label: Using academic vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use vocabulary typical of academic texts in their own writing to create precise information and convey abstract ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Write one paragraph on an academic topic that uses at least three academic vocabulary items accurately and appropriately.
nodes.typical_width: Select and use academic vocabulary appropriately in own writing across different topics, demonstrating understanding that academic vocabulary choices create a formal, precise register and convey abstract ideas accurately.
wider: Revise a piece of informal writing to use academic vocabulary appropriately, and analyse what changes in tone, precision and register as a result
Investigate how using academic vocabulary accurately signals membership in a discourse community — how vocabulary choices mark a writer as credible within academic contexts
Explore how students from language backgrounds other than English may have different relationships to academic vocabulary, and consider what strategies support vocabulary acquisition

response_modes.reason: Accurate use of academic vocabulary in writing requires repeated practice in authentic writing contexts. Students can identify academic vocabulary before they can deploy it fluently. Consolidation through multiple writing tasks — with feedback on precision of usage — builds the fluency needed.

success_criteria: Uses at least three academic vocabulary items accurately in a piece of own writing.
Word choices are appropriate to the academic register of the task — neither informal substitutes nor technical jargon used inappropriately.
